title: The Sacrifice at the Lu; the Memorial on Setting Out
summary: Coming home, the army cannot cross the Lu for the storm raised by the unburied dead. Told that the river wants forty-nine heads, Zhuge Liang has flour cakes stuffed with meat moulded into the shape of heads and thrown in instead, and the water goes down.

Then he submits the memorial: an account of a mat-weaver who called on him three times, an instruction to his lord's son about which ministers to trust, and a statement of intent. It is the most famous prose document in the language, and it ends with him unable to see the page for tears.
history: The memorial is real and survives entire. The novel quotes it at length and does not need to improve it.

pins.note: Submits the memorial, and marches north.
Told, in writing, which of his ministers to trust.
Over seventy, and refuses to be left behind.
